22 Four solid steel rods, each of length 2.0 m and cross-sectional area 250 mm2, equally support an
object weighing 10 kN. The weight of the object causes the rods to contract by 0.10 mm.
What is the Young modulus of steel?
A
2.0 × 108
N m–2
B
2.0 × 1011
N m–2
C
8.0 × 108
N m–2
D
8.0 × 1011
N m–2

hints: Notice the wording equally support - the $10 \text{ kN}$ weight is shared, so find the compressive force $F$ on one $2.0 \text{ m}$ rod.
Recall Young modulus as stress over strain, $E = (F/A)/(x/L) = FL/Ax$, with $A = 250 \text{ mm}^2$ and contraction $x = 0.10 \text{ mm}$.

Convert before substituting: $1 \text{ mm}^2 = 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2$ and $0.10 \text{ mm} = 1.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$, then compare stress of order $10^7 \text{ Pa}$ with strain of order $10^{-5}$.
walkthrough: Force is shared by four identical rods, so force on one rod is $F = 10000/4 = 2500 \text{ N}$ in compression. Young modulus has the same magnitude for compression as for extension.
State the rule $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain}$ where $\text{stress} = F/A$ and $\text{strain} = x/L$. Here $L = 2.0 \text{ m}$ and $x = 0.10 \text{ mm} = 1.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$.
Calculate stress $= 2500/(2.5 \times 10^{-4}) = 1.0 \times 10^7 \text{ N m}^{-2}$ and strain $= (1.0 \times 10^{-4})/2.0 = 5.0 \times 10^{-5}$ with no unit.
Calculate $E = (1.0 \times 10^7)/(5.0 \times 10^{-5}) = 2.0 \times 10^{11} \text{ N m}^{-2}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: Gives $2.0 \times 10^8 \text{ N m}^{-2}$, about 1000 times too small, from incorrect conversion of $250 \text{ mm}^2$ to $\text{m}^2$.

B.explanation: Uses force per rod of $2500 \text{ N}$, correct stress and strain to give $E = 2.0 \times 10^{11} \text{ N m}^{-2}$.

C.explanation: Gives $8.0 \times 10^8 \text{ N m}^{-2}$, from using the full $10 \text{ kN}$ on one rod and an area unit conversion error.

D.explanation: Gives $8.0 \times 10^{11} \text{ N m}^{-2}$, from using the full $10 \text{ kN}$ on one rod instead of dividing equally between the four rods.
